title: Investigate worker memory growth before scaling
raw_problem: Our background worker RSS grows from 600MB to 3GB over six hours and then gets OOM-killed. The quick fix suggested is doubling pod memory. Should we scale memory now or find the root cause first?
recommended_next_action: Run a bounded reproduction with heap/RSS sampling and queue-depth correlation, then compare memory growth on a fixed input batch against live traffic growth.
open_questions: Does memory grow with processed job count, queue depth, payload size, or wall-clock time?
Is the growth in heap, native memory, buffers, or child processes?
Does memory return after GC or worker restart on a fixed-size batch?
